accounting.rationale: R401 requires an initial pointer-decl and comma-separated subsequent items. R857, not a generic bare-name list, supplies each declaration.
Explicit R804/C810 defines a data object name and overrides assumed R402. This branch is not a component, element, section, function reference or procedure target.
The whole parenthesized shape may be absent. Its absence does not prove scalar rank: a compatible array declaration can supply rank separately, without a second explicit DIMENSION specification.

If the parentheses occur, R401 and R822 supply a nonempty comma list of colon-only shape specifications. Bound expressions, assumed size, assumed rank and coarray brackets are not this inline alternative. Canonical C834 also restricts pointer-array declarations.
The second alternative is a procedure-pointer entity name, not permission for a data pointer to change category or for a procedure name to acquire a data-array declarator.

The complete 502-head scan finds no explicit procptr-entity-name production; R402 therefore supplies its name syntax. C892 and C855 still require the actual EXTERNAL attribute, not necessarily an EXTERNAL keyword.

Preserve the R857 procedure-pointer alternative. An otherwise unclassified POINTER name can denote a data pointer; removing EXTERNAL alone is not automatically a negative. A data-pointer function result is not the named procedure-pointer subject.

8.5.9, a qualifying nonabstract/nonseparate interface body under15.4.3.2p5, or a procedure declaration under15.4.3.6p1 can supply EXTERNAL. C855 is the canonical general named-procedure constraint; one approved finite connection must not duplicate its execution.

Normative statement-to-attribute definition. Operational pointer association, target access, deferred parameters and procedure invocation retain8.5.14 and their defining mechanisms; there is no extra declaration-only S effect.
8.5.1p1 permits this attribute-specification route. C815 still applies to another explicit POINTER specification in the same scoping unit.
POINTER is not TARGET or ALLOCATABLE. C854 excludes those simultaneous attributes, INTRINSIC and coarray status; statement grammar does not waive those restrictions.
The property belongs to the listed data or procedure pointer entities, not to all similarly typed objects, their targets, or every component of a containing object.

PENDING finite relations to8.5.14 and to actual declaration, association, allocation, interface, host/use scope and lifetime owners. No case link, SourceUses approval, initialized status or passing runtime effect is created.
The example has a derived-type scalar and a rank-two deferred-shape data pointer. The fragment neither defines NODE nor initializes either pointer.
An illustrative declaration fragment, not a complete program or a new normative prohibition.
A completed example needs a legitimate visible NODE definition and the actual declared type of CURRENT. The chosen earlier type declaration is not a universal POINTER-before/after-type ordering rule.
CURRENT is a whole data object, not a component or the target of a pointer assignment. No payload or association inquiry is present.
The two deferred specifications declare A's rank here. They do not establish extents, a target, allocation or a defined association status.

requirements.title: A POINTER statement requires a pointer-declaration list
requirements.definition: POINTER is followed by an optional double colon and a nonempty comma-separated list of R857 pointer declarations. The items can use eligible data-object or procedure-pointer forms. The grammar does not establish association, replace the actual attribute/scope rules or require an EXTERNAL keyword on a data pointer.

pending.double-colon-form: PENDING compile/positive-control: a complete module with an explicitly typed ordinary INTEGER object p and POINTER :: p, with no POINTER type attribute, initialization, executable reference or status inquiry. This is a declaration admission, not an association effect.
pending.no-double-colon-form: PENDING the same complete module using POINTER p. Omit both colons together and retain required token separation; a one-colon form is not this alternative.
pending.mixed-data-procedure-list: PENDING complete compile control with an INTEGER data object p, an explicitly REAL/EXTERNAL procedure entity cb and POINTER :: p, cb. Each pointer attribute is specified once. No callback or pointer target is required merely for these unused declarations.
pending.missing-list-exclusion: PENDING complete bare and double-colon empty-list negatives, each repaired solely by appending an existing eligible data name. The surrounding module stays valid. A report of the premature terminator or failed required name may qualify only after independent source/control/location review; no fixed English phrase, generic EOF, unrelated name error or unsupported-declaration fallback is presumed sufficient.
pending.list-separator-repair: PENDING two distinct eligible names with a missing separating comma, and a separate trailing-comma form. Repair only the selected comma defect. Repeating one name would introduce C815 and is not a grammar witness.
pending.local-name-source: PENDING a finite source/scope relation to19.5.1.4p2: an object name in a POINTER statement is a local identifier in the relevant scoping unit. Do not infer mutation of a host entity or extend ordinary-subprogram locality claims indiscriminately to BLOCK, interface and use-associated contexts.
pending.single-specification-source: PENDING canonical C815 relations for one statement route versus a POINTER type/procedure attribute plus another explicit statement. Prior type declarations are isolation choices, not a universal ordering condition. A separate legitimate DIMENSION specification is not a second POINTER specification.
pending.attribute-owner-source: PENDING finite C854/C855 and R857/C892 relations retaining data/procedure category and actual EXTERNAL routes. No new generic pointer-assignment, allocation, C interoperability, pointer representation or lifetime witness is created.

requirements.oracle: Complete standalone-statement compile admissions and minimal syntax repairs. Validate actual entity categories, types, scope and single-attribute routes before interpreting an empty or malformed list. Canonical attribute and operational owners remain separate.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Required reporting is not fatal rejection, prescribed wording or a printed R856. Unsupported pointers, duplicate attributes, invalid shape, unresolved types/interfaces, wrong live origins, echo/context-only records and native failures do not prove the selected grammar cause. No allocation, association, initial disassociation or target-value effect is credited.

requirements.title: A pointer declaration names a data object with optional deferred shape or a procedure pointer
requirements.definition: The data alternative names a whole data object, optionally followed by a parenthesized nonempty list of deferred-shape specifications. R804/C810 supplies the object name and R822 supplies each colon-only shape specification. Without that inline shape, rank can be established elsewhere. The other alternative is a procedure-pointer entity name; its name grammar follows R402 and its actual EXTERNAL property is governed by C892/C855. A procedure's result rank is not a data-array declarator on the procedure pointer name.

pending.scalar-data-name: PENDING an actual scalar INTEGER data object with a single POINTER :: p statement and no shape, initializer, target or inquiry. The complete surrounding declarations establish scalar rank; omission of the inline suffix alone is not the oracle.
pending.inline-rank-one: PENDING a complete module with INTEGER :: p and POINTER :: p(:), with the inline list as the only explicit DIMENSION specification. Object compilation establishes admission, not extents or association.
pending.separately-declared-rank: PENDING INTEGER :: p(:,:) followed by POINTER :: p, so the rank is supplied once by the type declaration and omitted in the pointer statement. All complete declarations are considered together; do not add another inline shape and silently violate C815.
pending.procedure-pointer-name: PENDING the bare name cb in a POINTER statement with independently established procedure identity and EXTERNAL via an explicit declaration or another source-qualified route. It is not an arbitrary procedure target, callback invocation, function result or data object merely named cb.
pending.nonempty-shape-list: PENDING p() versus p(:) in otherwise identical data-pointer modules: inserting one colon repairs the empty list. Explicit bounds/assumed-size/assumed-rank alternatives require separately reviewed R822/C834 ownership rather than unexamined duplicate grammar credit.
pending.name-not-designator: PENDING a fully defined derived-type holder and POINTER :: holder%component contrasted with the eligible whole-object name holder, with the repair deleting only the component suffix and no preexisting POINTER attribute on holder. Other element/section forms need independent repairs that leave a genuine whole eligible object.
pending.procedure-array-branch-source: PENDING a finite R857/R804/C810 relationship for an explicitly EXTERNAL function-pointer name cb with cb(:), contrasted with bare cb. The parenthesized alternative requires a data object; if a processor parses that alternative, the wrong-entity cause belongs to C810 and is not automatically an isolated R857 syntax failure. Actual procedure identity and scalar result characteristics must remain fixed, with no reinterpretation as a data-pointer function result. Implement only after canonical ownership and a complete repair are independently established.
pending.shape-and-state-source: PENDING finite R822/C834/C815, scope and19.5.2 relationships. RANK-clause routes retain their separate eligibility; the inline syntax does not admit arbitrary bounds or declare pointer arrays with one independently associated pointer per element. No ASSOCIATED/value/bounds inquiry is made without its own defined-status/association premises.

requirements.oracle:
Observe complete compile admissions for each syntactic alternative and source-qualified minimal repairs for malformed declarators. Establish rank and data/procedure identity from the complete program, not spelling or omission alone; preserve canonical shape and state ownership.

Batch320 R857 attribute-statement fixtures: the rank-two deferred-shape data-pointer declaration is exercised through valid pointer association. The fixture directly asserts RANK/SIZE and payload after association; its feature mutant changes the pointer declaration and target to rank one so the rank assertion fails.
requirements.oracle_limitation:
No required English diagnostic or run-time trap follows from this numbered grammar rule. Correctly associated targets, target values, array extents and callback results need distinct runtime evidence. Unknown NODE, unsupported procedures, accidental data reclassification, wrong scope, duplicate attributes or native failures are not isolated R857 causes.

Batch320 R857 limits: only the rank-two deferred-shape data branch is covered with a runtime-distinguishable rank mutation. Scalar data, procedure-pointer names, rank-one, separately declared rank, malformed shape lists, procedure-array ambiguity, and finite source graph facets remain pending.

requirements.title: Procedure-pointer names in POINTER statements require EXTERNAL
requirements.definition: An entity selected through the procedure-pointer-name alternative of a POINTER statement must have the EXTERNAL attribute. That property can be supplied by a valid EXTERNAL specification, a qualifying interface body, or a procedure declaration; the keyword EXTERNAL need not occur literally. Removing one such keyword is not a violation if another route supplies the property or the resulting name simply denotes a legal data pointer. The general C855 requirement remains applicable to the same named procedure.

pending.external-statement-route: PENDING a complete module declaring cb as a REAL external procedure and then POINTER :: cb exactly once. Its known function type and actual EXTERNAL attribute are explicit. Prefer a reviewed finite connection to C855.pointer-statement-external over a clone of the same program; an occurrence may also supply R856/R857 admission only after its actual role is adjudicated. No initialization, target definition, call, object payload or linker dependency is introduced.
pending.nonabstract-interface-body-route: PENDING a complete specific, nonabstract, non-MODULE interface body for an ordinary callback and a separate POINTER :: cb statement. Under15.4.3.2p5 the interface body supplies EXTERNAL. Prefer the same actual canonical C855.interface-body-external witness through a reviewed finite connection rather than duplicate execution. ABSTRACT INTERFACE alone only defines a template, and a separate module procedure interface is not this route.
pending.procedure-declaration-route: PENDING a complete abstract interface signature and PROCEDURE(signature) :: cb followed by POINTER :: cb. The procedure declaration supplies EXTERNAL under15.4.3.6p1 and POINTER is specified only by the statement. The current C855 procedure-declaration plan instead spells POINTER as a procedure attribute, so it is not automatically an R857 statement witness. Choose one suitable canonical whole case and independently justify any reuse; no second EXTERNAL or POINTER specification, target, callback or ABI claim is needed.
pending.missing-external-report: PENDING an independently source-adjudicated whole-unit counterexample with procedure identity fixed and every EXTERNAL-conferring route absent. A possible lead is an empty module subroutine named in a POINTER statement in that same module; its control would retain the POINTER statement but replace the contained procedure definition with a qualifying ordinary specific interface body, thereby conferring EXTERNAL. This is not an approved witness: C855 overlap, same-scope identity, data/procedure ambiguity, the actual declaration-order conditions and the causal report must first be resolved. Merely deleting EXTERNAL can yield valid data-pointer syntax, removing POINTER alone does not demonstrate the repaired property, and INTRINSIC introduces C854.
pending.canonical-C855-source: PENDING an exact finite source/case connection to the general C855 named-procedure requirement. The witness must contain the R857 statement occurrence and preserve the actual named procedure, attribute, mode and role. No duplicate execution, automatic link approval or attribute-keyword grep proves the connection.
pending.association-and-characteristics-source: PENDING source relations to15.4.3.2/.6,10.2.2.4,15.5.2.10,8.5.14p4 and19.5.2. Procedure declaration does not establish association or permit an unassociated call. Any later initialization/invocation requires actual compatible characteristics, an eligible live target and the appropriate explicit interface.

requirements.oracle: Independently establish actual procedure identity and EXTERNAL provenance. Positive admissions distinguish the accepted specification routes; a negative requires a source-isolated missing property and an appropriate complete repair, not absence of a particular keyword. Reuse C855 evidence only through a reviewed finite connection.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Required reporting does not prescribe rejection or English wording. A legal data-pointer interpretation, EXTERNAL supplied elsewhere, a data-pointer function result, an intrinsic/POINTER conflict, a missing provider, unsupported procedure declaration or unrelated scope/type failure cannot stand in for the missing-EXTERNAL premise. No runtime or linked-effect evidence exists yet.

review_rationale: Batch320 bound reference-validated attribute-statement fixtures after two review rounds; seven frozen-LFortran failures (valid rank-2 POINTER, PROTECTED, inline TARGET array and VALUE statements rejected; C893 and two VOLATILE violations accepted) were independently confirmed as genuine.
